security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and documentation examples. Confirmed risks are remote installer execution through curl or PowerShell, direct GitHub installation, and a command that appends to ~/.bashrc.

remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell and PowerShell iex examples with package manager installs or verified download steps. Require explicit user confirmation before any remote script execution.
Do not append to ~/.bashrc automatically. Show the PATH change as an optional manual edit with rollback instructions.
When showing GitHub-based installation, explain source trust, pinning, and review of upstream changes before installing.

content.user_title: Manage Python Projects Faster with uv
content.value_statement: Python dependency management can be slow and inconsistent across tools. This skill shows uv workflows for projects, virtual environments, lockfiles, CI, and migrations.
actual_capabilities: Explains uv installation and verification options across common operating systems.
Shows how to create projects, add dependencies, and sync environments with uv.
Documents virtual environment workflows, Python version pinning, and uv run usage.
Covers lockfiles, frozen installs, offline installs, and dependency upgrade workflows.
Provides migration guidance from pip, Poetry, and pip-tools to uv.
Includes CI, Docker, pre-commit, VS Code, and monorepo workflow examples.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not install uv by itself.
Some installation examples require network access and trusted external sources.
It does not replace project-specific dependency review or lockfile auditing.
Version-specific uv behavior may change as uv evolves.

use_cases.title: Start a Python Service
use_cases.description: Create a uv project, pin Python, add runtime and test dependencies, and run commands through the managed environment.

use_cases.title: Speed Up CI Installs
use_cases.description: Use uv lockfiles, frozen sync, and cache-aware CI steps for faster and reproducible Python builds.

use_cases.title: Migrate Existing Tooling
use_cases.description: Move workflows from pip, Poetry, or pip-tools while preserving pyproject configuration and requirements compatibility.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic uv Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to plan a new Python project. Include project initialization, Python version pinning, dependency groups, and test commands.

prompt_templates.title: Convert pip Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to migrate my requirements-based Python project to uv. Explain the files to keep, commands to run, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI with uv
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to design a CI workflow for a Python project. Include lockfile use, dependency sync, testing, linting, and cache guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Advanced uv Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to review a Python monorepo workflow. Check workspace setup, lockfile strategy, Docker builds, offline mode, and migration risks.

output_examples.input: Plan a new FastAPI project that uses uv.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with project initialization, Python pinning, runtime dependencies, development tools, test execution, and lockfile practices.

output_examples.input: Help me migrate from Poetry to uv.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist that keeps the existing project metadata, syncs dependencies, verifies tests, and updates team documentation.

output_examples.input: Improve Python dependency installs in CI.
output_examples.output: A CI-focused recommendation covering uv setup, frozen installs, cache reuse, test commands, and lockfile consistency checks.

best_practices: Use lockfiles and frozen installs for reproducible environments.
Pin Python versions and run tools through uv-managed environments.
Review external install commands before execution, especially downloaded scripts.
anti_patterns: Running remote installer scripts without checking source trust or integrity.
Mixing unmanaged virtual environments with uv-managed project state.
Updating dependencies without reviewing lockfile changes and test results.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and explain uv workflows for Python projects, dependencies, virtual environments, lockfiles, CI, Docker, and migrations.

faq.question: Does the skill install uv automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples. Users should approve and run installation steps themselves.

faq.question: Can it replace pip, Poetry, or pip-tools?
faq.answer: It explains migration paths and equivalent uv workflows, but each project should test compatibility before changing tooling.

faq.question: Does it support CI and Docker workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for frozen installs, cache use, test commands, linting, and container dependency setup.

faq.question: What safety checks should I apply?
faq.answer: Review remote installer commands, prefer trusted package managers, verify sources, and inspect lockfile changes before committing.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
